commented.problem: The new initialization lock is keyed by the cloned session pointer, so parallel first calls for the same persisted session can still acquire separate anonymous cookies.
commented.problem_framing: The fix must protect the logical persisted session identity, not just one in-memory clone produced by a single runner call.
commented.root_cause: Normal runner/session-service flows may load separate `*session.Session` instances for the same logical session, and pointer identity does not collapse those clones into one lock scope.
commented.approach: The PR decouples anonymous A2A principals from context IDs and adds session-scoped cookie handling plus initialization locking.
commented.implementation_derivation: The race sits in the lock key for the exact critical section that should serialize first-cookie acquisition.
commented.solution_fit_assessment: The direction is correct, but the lock key must use durable session identity and reload or share the cookie inside the lock.
commented.alternative_designs: Key by app/user/session plus cookie scope, or place the initialization guard in the session service layer where persisted state can be re-read atomically.
commented.tradeoffs: A durable key can serialize more calls than pointer identity, but it is the necessary scope for principal consistency.
commented.design_assessment: The design addresses the right problem but still has a first-call concurrency hole.
